Let \(T_i=I-\frac12 e_i e_i^T H\). After two draws,

\[
\mathbb E[f(x_2)]=\frac12 x_0^T N(a)x_0,\qquad
N(a)=\mathbb E_{i,j}\bigl[T_i^T T_j^T H T_jT_i\bigr].
\]

A direct computation gives

\[
N=\begin{pmatrix}
\frac32-\frac{11}4a+\frac32a^2&\frac14a+\frac12a^2&-\frac12+\frac74a-\frac32a^2\\
\frac14a+\frac12a^2&\frac34a+\frac72a^2&\frac14a+\frac12a^2\\
-\frac12+\frac74a-\frac32a^2&\frac14a+\frac12a^2&\frac32-\frac{11}4a+\frac32a^2
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Thus \(R_2(a)\) is the largest generalized eigenvalue of \(N\) relative to \(H\).

By symmetry, split into the antisymmetric line \((1,0,-1)\) and the symmetric plane \((s,t,s)\).

For \((1,0,-1)\),

\[
\lambda_{\rm anti}(a)=1-\frac94a+\frac32a^2.
\]

On the symmetric plane, with basis \((1,0,1),(0,1,0)\), the generalized eigenvalues are the roots in \(\lambda\) of

\[
4\lambda^2+(-4+3a-10a^2)\lambda
+\frac32a+\frac{21}4a^2-8a^3-a^4=0.
\]

The larger symmetric root dominates the antisymmetric value for \(0<a<\frac12\), so we minimize that larger root. At an interior minimizer, the polynomial and its \(a\)-derivative vanish simultaneously. Eliminating \(\lambda\) gives

\[
F(a)=1856a^6+8512a^5+4460a^4+2268a^3-4269a^2+528a+108.
\]

The relevant stationary point is the unique zero of \(F\) in \((3/10,31/100)\); the other stationary point from the elimination belongs to the smaller symmetric eigenvalue. Since the larger root is \(1\) at both endpoints \(a=0,\frac12\), this interior point is the global minimizer.

\[
\boxed{
a=\operatorname{root}\!\left(
1856x^6+8512x^5+4460x^4+2268x^3-4269x^2+528x+108;\,
\frac{3}{10},\frac{31}{100}
\right)
}
\]

Numerically, \(a\approx 0.302839079\).
